name: GRANDProto300 (GRAND prototype)

placements.quote: 200 km² in the Gobi Desert near Xiaodushan, in northern Dunhuang, China
placements.note: Placed at the nearest named city (Dunhuang) as a coarse regional pointer only; see site:grandproto300-dunhuang for why no precise coordinate exists.

technology.value: Surface radio antenna array detecting the radio pulses from extensive air showers and Earth-skimming neutrino-induced showers
technology.quote: the array was extended to its current 65-antenna stage (GP300_s65), built south of GP13, covering an area of about 30 km².

intervals.label: GP300_s13
intervals.quote: In June 2023, the deployment of the 13-antenna stage, GP300_s13, was completed.

intervals.label: GP300_s65
intervals.quote: By April 2025, the array was extended to its current 65-antenna stage (GP300_s65)

station_count.quote: the array was extended to its current 65-antenna stage (GP300_s65)

area.quote: covering an area of about 30 km²
area.note: Design target for the full GRANDProto300 stage is 200 km².

notes: No source fetched this session gives a numeric coordinate for the precise Gobi Desert / Dunhuang array site (only 'near Xiaodushan, in northern Dunhuang, China'); the placement above points at the nearest named city (Dunhuang) as a coarse regional pointer rather than a surveyed array position, per A17's fallback rule.

summary.plain: A prototype radio antenna array in the Gobi Desert in China, testing the technology for a much bigger planned array to detect cosmic rays and neutrinos.
summary.technical: GRANDProto300 pathfinder array in the Gobi Desert near Dunhuang, China: grew from a 13-antenna stage (deployed 2023-06) to a 65-antenna stage covering ~30 km² (2025-04), validating the radio-detection approach for the full GRAND design.
